subject: series
synopsis: John Myung's Action Lab Comics series crossing over H.P. Lovecraft and Nikola Tesla in a shared adventure against Cthulhu Mythos threats in the early 20th century. A fun genre mashup that used the historical-figure crossover premise to good pulp-adventure effect.
author: John Myung

subject: series
synopsis: Yukie Nasu's shojo comedy set in the Greenwood all-male dormitory of Ryokuto Academy, where the sensitive Kazuya Hasukawa encounters an eccentric assortment of dormmates. A warm, charming series with excellent comic timing and character dynamics — a pioneer of dormitory/school slice-of-life manga.
author: Yukie Nasu

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Humphries' sci-fi adventure follows a courier and her mysterious passenger fleeing through parallel Earth dimensions, pursued by the powerful empire that controls interdimensional travel.
author: Sam Humphries

subject: series
synopsis: One of Clive Barker's Razorline titles at Marvel (1993-1994): a comedian-turned-hero battles supernatural forces.

subject: series
synopsis: A special 20th anniversary edition of Brad Meltzer and Rags Morales's landmark Identity Crisis miniseries, which shocked the DC Universe with the murder of Sue Dibny and dark revelations about the Justice League's past.
author: Brad Meltzer

subject: series
synopsis: Petos' slice-of-life follows a biology teacher fascinated by demi-humans who interviews the monster girls at his school about their unique experiences. A gentle, thoughtful series that uses its fantasy premise to explore disability and difference with empathy.
author: Petos

subject: series
synopsis: A team-up series pairing Jackpot (Mary Jane Watson as a new heroine) with Felicia Hardy's Black Cat in a crime-thriller adventure set in the Spider-Man corner of the Marvel Universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Jeffrey Brown's (Darth Vader and Son) charming all-ages graphic novel series about young Roan Novachez attending Jedi Academy, presented as a combination of diary entries, comics, letters, and school assignments. A pitch-perfect all-ages Star Wars comic that captures the school-days experience with affection and wit.
author: Jeffrey Brown

subject: series
synopsis: The graphic novel adaptation of Jim Butcher's first Dresden Files novel — Chicago wizard detective Harry Dresden investigating a magical murder — faithfully adapted by Mark Powers and Carlos Gomez.
author: Mark Powers

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Russ Braun's spy-parody follows a British super-spy who discovers all his illegitimate children are organizing to destroy him — a merciless skewering of the James Bond mythology.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Pulido's creation, Lady Death is a medieval noblewoman who becomes an iconic white-haired death goddess after a Faustian bargain; the series was a flagship of the early 1990s bad-girl comics movement and defined Chaos! Comics.
author: Brian Pulido

subject: series
synopsis: Sanpei Shirato's landmark ninja manga following Kamui, a low-born ninja who rejects his caste and fights for freedom against the rigid feudal hierarchy of Edo-era Japan. One of the foundational works of 1960s manga, deeply political and beautifully drawn, Kamui was a major cultural touchstone in Japan's counterculture movement.
author: Sanpei Shirato

subject: series
synopsis: A 1950s Charlton Comics series with lighthearted juvenile content.

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Koike and Noriyoshi Inoue's extremely violent and sexually explicit manga about Sleepy, a Japanese-American NYPD officer, and his brutish partner Mad Bull in a luridly over-the-top depiction of New York street crime. Notorious for its extreme content rather than its storytelling sophistication.
author: Kazuo Koike

subject: series
synopsis: Gene Ha's fantasy about a woman whose sister returns from a fantastic world she thought was imaginary, bringing dangerous creatures with her. Ha's detailed, joyful linework is the main attraction.
author: Gene Ha

subject: series
synopsis: J.M. DeMatteis and Todd Nauck's 2023 Magneto mini, set during his early days as headmaster of the New Mutants.

subject: series
synopsis: Skottie Young and Clay Mann's 2012 Magneto: Not a Hero: after Schism, Magneto hunts a resurrected clone committing atrocities in his name.
author: Skottie Young

subject: series
synopsis: Neil Gaiman and Andy Kubert's 2003 Marvel Elseworlds-style miniseries transplanting the Marvel superhero universe to Elizabethan England of 1602, with Nick Fury serving Elizabeth I while a new world of emerging 'witchbreed' challenges the era's religious authority. One of Marvel's finest prestige projects — Gaiman's historical fiction sensibility meets Marvel mythology with elegantly conceived results.
author: Neil Gaiman

subject: series
synopsis: Karl Kesel's comedic story of a Marvel Universe populated entirely by apes, a self-aware parody of superhero excess.
author: Karl Kesel

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel anthology showcasing new characters (Guardians of the Galaxy debuted here!) and reprint material. Historically significant as an incubator.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's all-ages adaptation of the Guardians of the Galaxy animated series, presenting accessible adventures of Star-Lord, Rocket, Groot, Gamora, and Drax for younger readers. Consistent with the fun, accessible tone of the animation.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: IDW/DC's comic series adapting the classic He-Man and the Masters of the Universe characters, bringing the Eternia mythology to comics readers and tying into DC Universe continuity during some runs.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: The flagship Mickey Mouse anthology presenting Floyd Gottfredson's adventure newspaper strips and stories by other creators, showcasing the Mouse as a genuine action hero in elaborate globetrotting adventures.
author: Floyd Gottfredson

subject: series
synopsis: John Rozum's supernatural mystery series follows a husband-and-wife team of paranormal investigators — Adam and Julie Kadmon — in a small Connecticut town with a surprising history of the occult.
author: John Rozum

subject: series
synopsis: Akira Sugito's 2022 manga about Momo, a young vampire who feeds on desire rather than blood, navigating relationships with humans while concealing her supernatural nature. A romantic horror manga with a distinctive visual style.
author: Akira Sugito

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Casey and Ed McGuinness' 1999 WildStorm series following Mr. Majestic — a Superman-like ultra-powerful alien — in stories that deliberately contrasted his omnipotent problem-solving with the nuanced ethics of WildStorm's darker universe. Casey's sharp writing and McGuinness' gorgeous art made this a cult favorite.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series featuring Kamala Khan as Ms. Marvel in episodic adventures formatted for the Marvel Unlimited platform.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's Infinity Comics digital series adapting and expanding Kamala Khan's early Ms. Marvel stories in a format optimized for mobile reading on Marvel Unlimited.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Brandon Graham's surreal road-trip fantasy follows a smuggler and her werewolf boyfriend through a beautiful post-Soviet dreamscape.
author: Brandon Graham

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Michael Avon Oeming's alternate history thriller in which organized crime won the battle for America in the 1930s. Ambitious premise with Oeming's bold graphic style.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's anthology series pairing different MLP characters in standalone team-up adventures, with rotating creative teams adding variety to the ongoing Friendship is Magic mythology. All-ages stories for fans of the animated series.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Rick Remender's Image Comics series about a scientist who created the ultimate weapon — his children, engineered to be indestructible soldiers — and the consequences when they go off-script.
author: Rick Remender

subject: series
synopsis: New Avengers facing A.I.M. threat. Excellent villain showcase and team dynamics.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Baron and Steve Rude's science fiction superhero series — one of the great independent comics of the 1980s — following Horatio Hellpop, a man driven by alien dreams to execute mass murderers, who becomes a reluctant god-like figure harboring fugitives in space.
author: Mike Baron

subject: series
synopsis: A Lion Forge Comics tie-in to the controversial 1992 FMV video game Night Trap, one of the titles that helped spark the Senate hearings that led to the ESRB ratings system.
author: Cullen Bunn

subject: series
synopsis: Ben Dunn's early creator-owned series from Antarctic Press blending high school comedy, ninjas, aliens, and anime-style action in an early American manga-influenced work. One of the foundational books of the American manga movement of the late 1980s, notable for predating the mainstream manga boom by a decade.

subject: series
synopsis: Sean McKeever's limited series featuring Spider-Girl and the Avengers Academy students confronting a new Onslaught entity in a story that connected to the Shadow Land era. A competent tie-in with good handling of its teen hero cast.
author: Sean McKeever

subject: series
synopsis: A sci-fi action miniseries featuring a female android soldier protagonist in a dark future war scenario.

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Kirkman and Paul Azaceta's horror series following Kyle Barnes, a man who has been plagued by demonic possession since childhood, as he partners with a reverend to investigate a growing supernatural evil in a small West Virginia town.
author: Robert Kirkman

subject: series
synopsis: An early AC Comics publication from 1969-1975, predating the company's full focus on golden age revival and female superheroes, representing AC's origins as a small press publisher.

subject: series
synopsis: Fantagraphics' complete hardcover reprint of Charles Schulz's Peanuts Sunday pages in restored color, five years per volume.
author: Charles Schulz

subject: series
synopsis: Suu Minazuki's manga about a post-apocalyptic world where everyone has a number tattoo on their body that counts up or down based on their 'count' — a metric tied to their worth and power. An elaborate world-building exercise with action and dark themes.
author: Suu Minazuki

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's reprints of Bud Sagendorf's 1940s-50s Dell Popeye comic books, restored and recoloured.

subject: series
synopsis: Kyle Higgins and Marcelo Costa's superhero drama follows a failed writer who returns home in debt and stumbles into a cosmic power suit, building an emotionally grounded modern superhero universe with clear Kamen Rider DNA.
author: Kyle Higgins

subject: series
synopsis: A GFT universe series following Red Agent, a character connected to the Red Riding Hood mythology, now operating as a supernatural operative dealing with threats to the human world. Part of Zenescope's expanding character roster.

subject: series
synopsis: An indie action series with emphasis on character development and emotional stakes.

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis's gritty sequel to Red Team follows the surviving members of an NYPD undercover unit as they face the violent fallout of their earlier crimes. A taut, character-driven crime story with Ennis's trademark moral ambiguity and unflinching brutality.
author: Garth Ennis

subject: series
synopsis: Geoff Johns and Bryan Hitch's 2024 Image Comics series about a British soldier from the Revolutionary War era rendered immortal — forced to observe and occasionally interfere with American history across 250 years. A John's-style slow mythology-builder with Hitch's grand cinematic art.
author: Geoff Johns

subject: series
synopsis: A horror anthology series produced in partnership with musician Rob Zombie, mixing pulp horror vignettes with Zombie's signature grindhouse aesthetic. More a curiosity than a standout comic, but competently executed schlocky horror.
author: Rob Zombie

subject: series
synopsis: Ryan Parrott's Boom Studios Power Rangers story following the original Rangers directly after the events of their first encounter with Rita Repulsa, exploring their private lives and the emotional cost of their secret.
author: Ryan Parrott

subject: series
synopsis: Detective series following Sam Burke and Twitch Williams, the homicide detectives from the Spawn universe, as they investigate supernatural and mundane crimes.
author: Todd McFarlane

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Michael Bendis and Alex Maleev's political thriller about a young woman who, after being traumatized by police corruption, starts a revolution. Maleev's photo-realistic art lends urgency; the political anger feels genuine.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Hellboy-universe Victorian-era spinoff following occult investigator Sir Edward Grey, atmospheric and well-crafted.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Harris and Martin Morazzo's dystopian science fiction series set in a near-future ice age where climate-controlling technology has failed, following an eco-terrorist who may hold the key to restoring the world's weather.
author: Joe Harris

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Baylis's autobiographical anthology: short slice-of-life stories about his own life, each drawn by a different indie artist.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Azzarello and Eduardo Risso's 2011 Vertigo series set in a future where genetically engineered people called Spacemen — built for outer space but now abandoned on Earth — struggle to survive in a flooded, media-saturated world. A dense, difficult, rewarding sci-fi noir from one of comics' best crime-fiction teams.
author: Brian Azzarello

subject: series
synopsis: A Spawn spin-off series involving Spawn facing a being capable of killing gods, part of the ongoing Spawn mythology. Features the intense supernatural action the franchise is known for.
author: Brian Holguin

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2023 Flash family anthology series spotlighting various Speed Force characters — Avery Ho, Max Mercury, Wally West's kids — as they navigate the expanded Flash mythology of the Infinite Frontier era.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2007 anthology series featuring stories about Spider-Man and his supporting cast and family, connecting various Spider-characters in standalone short stories across the Spider-Man universe.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Walter Simonson's classic space opera characters, collected and expanded by IDW. Originally serialized in Heavy Metal and Epic Illustrated, the Star Slammers are elite mercenary warriors in a universe of galactic conflict — Simonson's character design and epic-scale action at their most ambitious.
author: Walter Simonson

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's all-ages Halloween-themed Star Wars anthology, framing spooky standalone tales around Vader's foreboding castle on Mustafar.
author: Cavan Scott

subject: series
synopsis: A 2024 Marvel miniseries depicting the New Republic's military campaign to retake Jakku from Imperial holdouts in the weeks following the Battle of Endor, serving as the lead-in to the broader Battle of Jakku event.

subject: series
synopsis: Alyssa Wong's Marvel series follows the rogue archaeologist Doctor Aphra, a morally flexible scoundrel chasing dangerous relics across the galaxy while dodging the consequences of her own schemes. A fan-favorite Star Wars antihero showcase.
author: Alyssa Wong

subject: series
synopsis: Collections of New 52 Action Comics (2011-2016): Grant Morrison and Rags Morales's young, populist Superman, then Andy Diggle, Greg Pak and Aaron Kuder.

subject: series
synopsis: An ongoing series starring Jon Kent, Clark Kent's son, as the new Superman of Earth, written by Tom Taylor with art by John Timms. Jon grapples with his father's legacy while tackling modern social issues and eventually comes out as bisexual in a landmark issue.
author: Tom Taylor

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology series from TKO Studios collecting short-form graphic stories across genres from various creators, showcasing the publisher's commitment to bold, diverse voices and high-production literary comics.

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Jordan's New 52 Team 7 series following a covert team of DC's most dangerous operatives — Steve Trevor, Slade Wilson, Dinah Drake, and others — on black ops missions before the dawn of the superhero age.
author: Justin Jordan

subject: series
synopsis: A digital-first Infinite Comic crossover starring Spider-Man and Silk as they face a shared threat born from their unique radioactive spider-bite connection, formatted for mobile vertical reading.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Silver Age team-up series arising when both The Atom and Hawkman's solo titles were cancelled and combined. A curiosity of 1960s DC publishing economics that gave the two heroes a shared home, producing competent Silver Age adventure stories.
author: Bob Haney

subject: series
synopsis: Robert Rodi's 2003 CrossGen comedy: a suburban family whose members each get pulled into a different CrossGen genre, from sword-and-sorcery to space opera.

subject: series
synopsis: Jamie S. Rich and George Kambadais's Monkeybrain series about a teenage girl who inherits the identity of a superhero and must navigate the double life that comes with it. Bright, character-driven superhero comics with strong art and an appealing lead.
author: Jamie S. Rich

subject: series
synopsis: Donny Cates and Daniel Warren Johnson's action thriller follows a driver transporting unknown cargo for powerful people — and the soldiers hunting him across the country to stop the delivery.
author: Donny Cates

subject: series
synopsis: Otto Soglow's classic newspaper comic strip featuring a wordless diminutive monarch navigating absurd royal situations, notable for its minimalist art style and pantomime humor. The strip ran from 1934 and is considered a distinguished example of the silent comic strip tradition.
author: Otto Soglow

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's black-and-white magazine series featuring longer Hulk stories in the more permissive magazine format, set in the period between the Hulk's original series and his later appearances. Notable for early Bill Mantlo and Walt Simonson contributions.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Tyler James's ComixTribe superhero mystery series reworks Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None with a cast of superheroes, picking off its A-list of DC/Marvel analogues one by one in a whodunit that deconstructs the genre.

subject: series
synopsis: AWA's flagship superhero universe launch: a global plague kills millions, but some survivors gain extraordinary powers. Society's response — fear, militarization, exploitation — drives a story that is more political thriller than traditional superhero fare.
author: J.M. DeMatteis

subject: series
synopsis: Ben Edlund's Tick Comics mini-series Karma Tornado, continuing the absurdist superhero parody of the beloved New England City hero and his sidekick Arthur in darkly comic standalone adventures. Maintains the gleeful nonsense energy that made The Tick a cult classic.
author: Ben Edlund

subject: series
synopsis: Warren Ellis and Jon Davis-Hunt's brilliant 2017 Wildstorm relaunch — a complete reconstruction of the Wildstorm Universe from scratch, building a paranoid techno-conspiracy thriller with Jenny Sparks, Angela Spica, and a web of secrets.
author: Warren Ellis

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV and Michael Dialynas' mysterious survival horror follows a Wisconsin high school and all its students who are suddenly teleported to an alien forest, learning to survive its predators while uncovering its secrets.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Art Baltazar and Franco's utterly charming all-ages series reimagining the Teen Titans (and half the DC universe) as elementary school children having non-threatening adventures at Sidekick City Elementary. Multiple Eisner Award winner for Best Publication for Early Readers.
author: Art Baltazar

subject: series
synopsis: Donna Troy's death leads to the dissolution of Young Justice and a new Teen Titans.
author: Judd Winick

subject: series
synopsis: Akiko Higashimura's (Princess Jellyfish) comedy-drama about three women in their early thirties — a manga writer, a hair stylist, and a nail artist — navigating careers, romance, and the fear that life is passing them by. Higashimura's sharp wit and observational insight into women's social pressures made it one of the 2010s' most widely discussed josei manga.
author: Akiko Higashimura

subject: series
synopsis: Eiichi Shimizu and Tomohiro Shimoguchi's manga reimagining of the classic Ultraman tokusatsu hero for a modern audience, following Shinjiro Hayata — son of the original Ultraman — who inherits his father's legacy as a new Ultraman. A stylish, action-heavy take that treats the franchise with serious science-fiction intentions.
author: Eiichi Shimizu

subject: series
synopsis: A stylish European western following Jonas Crow, a cynical undertaker in the American frontier whose profession brings him into contact with violence, greed, and moral ambiguity at every turn. Ralph Meyer's stunning artwork and Xavier Dorison's sharp writing make this one of the best modern western BDs.
author: Xavier Dorison

subject: series
synopsis: Yumi Unita's heartwarming manga about 30-year-old bachelor Daikichi Kawachi, who impulsively takes in Rin, his grandfather's illegitimate young daughter after the family refuses responsibility for her. A rare manga focused entirely on the quiet joys and challenges of parenting, drawn with disarming simplicity and emotional generosity.
author: Yumi Unita

subject: series
synopsis: Ryosuke Asakura's manga following a socially isolated student chosen by nine Valkyries to strengthen their powers through love, blending Norse mythology with romantic comedy tropes. Primarily fan-service oriented with occasional genuine character moments.
author: Ryosuke Asakura

subject: series
synopsis: An action-focused Vampirella series featuring the iconic horror heroine unleashing hell against supernatural threats. Typical of Dynamite's modern Vampirella output: pulpy horror-action with a strong female lead.

subject: series
synopsis: A tie-in miniseries to the Venom War crossover event following Spider-Man's involvement in the conflict between symbiote factions, expanding the street-level consequences of the larger alien war.

subject: series
synopsis: Boom Studios' comic adaptation of Pixar's acclaimed animated film, extending the story of the lonely waste-collecting robot and his adventures with EVE in a future where Earth has been abandoned by humanity.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's Bronze Age horror anthology featuring spooky standalone tales with twist endings in the tradition of EC Comics, part of the wave of horror anthology titles DC published in the early 1970s following the relaxation of Comics Code restrictions.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A series of What If? stories exploring alternate outcomes of Avengers vs. X-Men, including scenarios where different characters received the Phoenix Force; uneven but entertaining for fans of the parent event.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: A mature-readers Wolverine miniseries with heightened violence as Logan pursues vengeance, the Red Band label signaling a return to the grittier, more brutal interpretation of the character.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Kazuo Koike and Ryoichi Ikegami's violent crime epic about a former mercenary seeking revenge in the jungles of South America, with Ikegami's uncompromising figure work at its most visceral.
author: Kazuo Koike

subject: series
synopsis: Matt Kindt's 2017 X-O Manowar: Aric of Dacia, retired on an alien world, is drawn back into war and rises from soldier to emperor.

subject: series
synopsis: James Tynion IV's horror series about a monstrous intelligence lurking beneath the internet, tapping into fears of technology, viral horror, and digital apocalypse.
author: James Tynion IV

subject: series
synopsis: Delcourt's French fantasy series: each album follows one of the Master Inquisitors, magically gifted investigators in a war-torn medieval world.

subject: series
synopsis: Annual special issues for the Punisher series from the late Bronze Age / early Copper Age, featuring extended standalone stories of Frank Castle's violent war on crime outside the regular continuity.
author: Mike Baron

subject: series
synopsis: Hideaki Sorachi's Gintama: in an Edo-period Japan conquered by aliens, lazy samurai Gintoki Sakata runs an odd-jobs business in a gag-heavy parody that swings into serious arcs.

subject: series
synopsis: Comic strips and stories based on the viral internet meme cat, delivering all-ages humor and grumpy observational comedy in a licensed format appealing to fans of the phenomenon.

subject: series
synopsis: An Action Lab Entertainment horror-action series about a comic store employee who bonds with demonic blades from an old B-movie comic and gains violent supernatural powers, known for its cheesecake covers and exploitation-film energy.

subject: series
synopsis: Mike Mignola and Scott Allie's Dark Horse ongoing follows Abe Sapien's solo journey through an apocalyptic America after he separates from the B.P.R.D. A meditative, beautifully drawn companion series to the wider Mignolaverse, valued by fans for its slower, more personal exploration of Abe's alien nature and identity.
author: Mike Mignola, Scott Allie

subject: series
synopsis: Mario Gully's independent Image series following Hannah Washington, a single mother who becomes the armored hero Ant through a traumatic near-death experience. A creator-owned superhero story driven by genuine personal investment from Gully.
author: Mario Gully

subject: series
synopsis: An omnibus collection of Jeff Lemire's acclaimed Black Hammer universe, gathering the deconstructionist superhero saga in one volume.
author: Jeff Lemire

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2001 Deadman series: Boston Brand's restless ghost possesses the living to set things right.

subject: series
synopsis: Jonathan Hickman and Sanford Greene's 2024 oversized one-shot: Doctor Doom confronts the death of the universe.

subject: series
synopsis: A martial arts fighter teams up with a young boy on a quest through a world of tournament fighters and dark supernatural forces in this French manga-influenced action series with superb fight choreography.
author: Balak / Vivès / Sanlaville

subject: series
synopsis: Various Sabretooth solo series from Marvel, the most notable being Larry Hama's 1993 miniseries establishing Sabretooth's origin in detail, followed by Daniel Way's later series. The character's extended mythology — his rivalry with Wolverine, his time as a Weapon X subject — was largely built in these pages.
author: Larry Hama

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Milligan and Chris Bachalo's psychedelic Vertigo series following Rac Shade, an alien wielding the Madness Vest, traversing a surreal America. Known for Bachalo's distinctive art and Milligan's surrealist writing.
author: Peter Milligan

subject: series
synopsis: Frank Miller and Chris Claremont's landmark 1982 Wolverine limited series, set in Japan and establishing the character's samurai code and love for Mariko Yashida. Defined the character's lone-wolf identity and remains one of the finest X-Men-adjacent stories.
author: Larry Hama

subject: series
synopsis: Kieron Gillen and Luca Maresca's 2024 X-Men Forever, sister book to Rise of the Powers of X, concluding his Krakoa-era threads.
author: Kieron Gillen

subject: series
synopsis: IDW's digital collection of Berkeley Breathed's Bloom County (1980-1989): Opus the penguin, Milo, Binkley and Bill the Cat in Pulitzer-winning satire.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's 2025 one-shot marking the new Ultimate Universe's first year and setting up its next phase.

subject: series
synopsis: Torunn Grønbekk's 2024 Carnage ongoing: the symbiote, free of Cletus Kasady, hunts for new hosts.

subject: series
synopsis: Powers' 2015 eight-issue volume, 'All the New Powers', with Walker and Pilgrim facing a new generation of powered criminals.
author: Brian Michael Bendis

subject: series
synopsis: Jed MacKay and Alessandro Cappuccio's 2021 Moon Knight: Marc Spector runs the Midnight Mission, protecting travelers of the night as Khonshu's fist.
author: Jed MacKay

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2012 digital-first Legends of the Dark Knight: out-of-continuity Batman stories by rotating creators, collected in print.

subject: series
synopsis: Duane Swierczynski's 2012 Valiant relaunch of Bloodshot: a nanite-powered soldier learns his memories are implants created by Project Rising Spirit.

subject: series
synopsis: Casey Gilly's apocalyptic future tale follows an elderly Buffy as the last surviving Slayer in a post-supernatural world, rediscovering her purpose in her twilight years.
author: Casey Gilly

subject: series
synopsis: Margaret Stohl's 2017 legacy-numbered Captain Marvel (#125-129), Carol Danvers back on Earth after her Alpha Flight station era.

subject: series
synopsis: Brian Azzarello and Carlos D'Anda's 2006 Deathblow: the supposedly dead Michael Cray returns home with no memory of how he survived.

subject: series
synopsis: Justin Gray and Jimmy Palmiotti's 2010 Freedom Fighters: Uncle Sam's team of Miss America, Human Bomb, Phantom Lady and others guards America.

subject: series
synopsis: Sterling Gates and Rob Liefeld's New 52 Hawk & Dove: Hank Hall and Dawn Granger as avatars of war and peace.

subject: series
synopsis: Joe Keatinge and Richard Elson's 2013 Morbius: the Living Vampire hides in a poor neighborhood and tries to do good.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's Red Sonja: the She-Devil with a Sword's sword-and-sorcery adventures; files mostly Michael Avon Oeming's 2005 relaunch.

subject: series
synopsis: Paul Jenkins and John Romita Jr.'s 2005 Sentry: Robert Reynolds battles his own dark side, the Void, after joining the New Avengers.

subject: series
synopsis: The ongoing Steven Universe comic series following the beloved animated show's characters in new all-ages adventures.

subject: series
synopsis: Peter Tomasi and Patrick Gleason's Rebirth Superman: Clark, Lois and son Jon Kent raise a family in rural Hamilton County, a warm father-and-son run.

subject: series
synopsis: Tom DeFalco and Ron Frenz's 2010 Thunderstrike mini: Kevin Masterson, son of the late Eric, inherits his father's mace.

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Priest's continuing Vampirella (2024, legacy #666+): the Drakulon-born vampire heroine in a dense, satirical horror saga.

subject: series
synopsis: Adam Warlock's 1972 series: Roy Thomas and Gil Kane's Counter-Earth messiah allegory, then from #9 Jim Starlin's cosmic Magus saga.

subject: series
synopsis: Jim Zub and Jon Malin's 2016 Thunderbolts: Winter Soldier leads Moonstone, Fixer, Mach-X and Atlas alongside the living Cosmic Cube Kobik.

subject: series
synopsis: 2000 AD's hardback annuals (1978-1990) and later yearbooks: Dredd, Strontium Dog and other strips plus features.

subject: series
synopsis: Gerry Duggan's 2015 Deadpool: a world-famous Deadpool hires a team of Mercs for Money; files hold Joe Kelly's 1998-99 issues.

subject: series
synopsis: Fleetway/Quality's US reprints of 2000 AD's Judge Dredd (1987-), coloured for American readers.

subject: series
synopsis: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo part 4: Josuke Higashikata and friends uncover the Stand users, including serial killer Yoshikage Kira, hiding in the quiet town of Morioh.

subject: series
synopsis: Hirohiko Araki's JoJo part 5: Giorno Giovanna, son of Dio, joins a Neapolitan gang aiming to topple the secretive Boss of Passione.

subject: series
synopsis: Dynamite's 2007 Savage Tales anthology of sword-and-sorcery stories featuring Red Sonja and other barbarians.

subject: series
synopsis: Takahiro's prequel to Akame ga Kill!: young Akame trained as an Imperial assassin before her defection to Night Raid.

subject: series
synopsis: John Carpenter and Anthony Burch's 2017 sequel: an elderly Jack Burton travels to a post-apocalyptic future ruled by the sorcerer Qing Wu.

subject: series
synopsis: Mad Cave Studios' 2024 Flash Gordon revival: Flash, Dale and Zarkov against Ming the Merciless on Mongo.

subject: series
synopsis: Benjamin Percy's 2025 Hellverine ongoing: Logan bonded with the demon Bagra-Ghul, a fusion of Wolverine and Ghost Rider.

subject: series
synopsis: Marvel's digital Infinite Comic based on the Ultimate Spider-Man animated series.

subject: series
synopsis: Jeph Loeb and Joe Madureira's 2008 Ultimates 3: the team investigates the Scarlet Witch's murder in a follow-up to Millar and Hitch.

subject: series
synopsis: Vertigo's 1997 four-issue revival of Weird War Tales: supernatural war stories by top creators.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Waid and Dan Mora's 2025 Justice League Unlimited: the Watchtower opens its doors to every hero on Earth in a sprawling, optimistic League.
author: Mark Waid
